title: Canonical provenance and rollback flow for quant artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Define and implement a deterministic provenance and versioning scheme for quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8) produced by calibration workflows, enable reproducible validation, and provide safe rollback semantics for serving runtime and Dedicated/Private deployments.
background: We currently produce quantization profiles and calibration artifacts as part of model onboarding and optimization, but artifact lineage is incomplete: artifacts lack a canonical content hash, environment fingerprint, and immutable provenance metadata. This complicates validating accuracy regressions, reproducing calibration runs, and performing safe rollbacks when a quant profile causes quality or performance regressions in production.
goals: 1) Introduce an immutable artifact package format with content hashing and signature. 2) Capture full provenance metadata: calibration script/version, random seeds, dataset snapshots (id + hash), tokenizer version, framework (PyTorch) + CUDA + cuDNN + OS fingerprints, quantization parameters, date and author. 3) Store artifacts in an immutable registry with semantic versioning and allow lookup by hash or tag. 4) Provide a reproducible CI job that replays calibration and independent accuracy validation, producing validation reports with deterministic metrics. 5) Implement runtime-compatible rollback and compatibility checks to ensure model-server mapping consistency.
acceptance_criteria:
- An artifact package (.rqf) spec is documented in the Confluence design doc and approved by ML infra and runtime.
- Upload workflow computes a canonical SHA-256 content hash covering weights, profile, and provenance metadata; artifact is stored in artifact-registry with hash and human tag.
- Artifact metadata includes environment fingerprint: PyTorch x.y.z, CUDA xx.y, cuDNN, OS distro and kernel, Python version, and hashes for any calibration datasets.
- CI job `quant-replay` can re-run calibration from artifact provenance and reproduce the quant profile hash end-to-end within 0.1% bit-for-bit-equivalent values for deterministic parts and within tolerance for floating ops.
- Serving runtime accepts artifacts by content-hash and rejects mismatched architecture/shape or incompatible kernel requirements.
- Rollback API allows mapping from serving route to previously-deployed artifact hash and revert within the same release without manual migration more than 10 minutes per service.
- Security review completed and signing keys stored in KMS; artifacts are signed during registration.
design_summary: Propose a single artifact package format (Redwood Quant Package - RQP) that bundles: canonicalized quant profile JSON, calibration metadata, model weight references (either embedded or a content-addressed pointer), validation report, and cryptographic signature. The package will include a manifest version and compute a canonical SHA-256 over a deterministic serialization (sorted keys, normalized floats to IEEE decimal string canonicalization where applicable). We will use a two-phase registry: a write-once object store (S3 with object immutability flags) plus an index service that maps tags -> content-hash and stores metadata. The index service exposes APIs for lookup by hash, tag, model name, and release. Runtime will fetch artifacts by hash; rollout controller will validate compatibility matrix before applying an artifact to a runtime pool.
implementation_notes:
- Serialization: use canonical JSON (sorted keys, consistent float formatting) and then compute SHA-256. Avoid embedding timestamps that vary; store timestamps as metadata fields excluded from hash to keep the content hash stable for identical artifacts produced later.
- Provenance fields: calibration script git SHA, container image SHA, pip freeze, dataset id + checksum, RNG seed(s), tokenizer git SHA.
- Registry: `s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/{hash}.rqp` plus DynamoDB/Spanner index entry with metadata. Use S3 Object Lock + KMS encryption.
- Signature: sign the computed content hash with Redwood artifact-signing key stored in KMS; attach signature to package.
- CI: add `quant-replay` and `quant-validate` pipeline steps to `infra-ci` that pull artifact by hash and re-run calibration/validation on a pinned container image to compare accuracy metrics.
- Runtime checks: add pre-deploy compatibility step that verifies model architecture hash matches artifact's expected shape and required kernel features (e.g., FP8 support) list.
- Backward compatibility: keep a translation shim that maps legacy profile formats into RQP on ingest so older artifacts can be content-hashed and stored without breaking existing serving contracts.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for canonical serializer and hash calculation with fixtures for floating edge cases.
- End-to-end test: register an artifact from a calibration run, then run `quant-replay` CI on an isolated infra job that should reproduce the same profile hash or produce equivalent validation metrics.
- QA: create synthetic regression where a quant profile with an intentional miscalibration is registered to a staging runtime; verify detection in the validation dashboard and initiate rollback.
- Load tests: publish/lookup 10k artifacts and measure registry indexing latency and storage costs.
- Security tests: verify signature verification in ingestion path and that revoked signing keys prevent new registrations.
rollback_procedure:
- Every deployment records the artifact hash and index entry. To rollback: 1) Use rollout controller to switch traffic to previous artifact hash for route. 2) Controller runs compatibility check to ensure target artifact meets runtime kernel requirements; if incompatible, abort and surface remediation steps. 3) If traffic switch is allowed, the controller performs canary traffic shift then 100% shift and marks the route tag to the previous hash. 4) Emit an audit event linking the rollback to the original deployment and reason.
- Emergency manual rollback: operators may call `/api/runtime/v1/rollback?route=<>&to_hash=<hash>` which triggers the same flow but requires 2 on-call approvals and an incident tag.
- Post-rollback: schedule `quant-replay` validation to determine root cause and optionally start a recalibration job with tightened validation thresholds.
